client_need: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
stem: A barcode medication administration system alerts the nurse that the scanned medication does not match the client’s active order. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Stop and resolve the mismatch before administering the medication.
options.B: Override the alert routinely because barcode alerts are often inconvenient.
options.C: Administer the medication first and investigate the alert at the end of the shift.
options.D: Bypass barcode scanning for the rest of the shift to prevent alert fatigue.

rationale: Barcode medication administration is intended to intercept patient–medication mismatches before administration. AHRQ notes that workarounds and routine bypasses degrade the safety benefit of barcoding and are associated with medication administration errors. A mismatch should therefore be resolved before administration.
educational_objective: Respond appropriately to a BCMA mismatch and avoid unsafe workarounds.
source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality, PSNet
source_locator: Barcode medication administration—error prevention; workarounds undermine effectiveness and increase medication-error risk
source_claim_supported: BCMA helps prevent medication administration errors; bypassing or working around the system undermines that safety function.
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
correction_summary: Changed the original vague override-attitude item to a concrete mismatch requiring resolution before administration.
audit_findings: Correct action follows the safety function of BCMA.
All other options are workarounds that bypass a safety alert.
Independent second pass found no alternative best action.
